notes: Colorado starts from federal taxable income (DR 0104 line 1: 'Enter your federal taxable income from your federal income tax form 1040, 1040 SR, or 1040 SP, line 15', booklet PDF p.8); additions on lines 2-9, subtractions from DR 0104AD on line 11, Colorado taxable income on line 12 (PDF p.10; form PDF p.39-40).

The booklet prints no standard deduction, personal exemption, dependent exemption, or age-65 or blindness amount of its own; base.deductions is empty. Federal deductions reach Colorado through federal taxable income.

Standard or itemized federal deduction addback (DR 0104 line 4, PDF p.8-9): when federal AGI (Form 1040 line 11a) exceeds 300,000, add back the part of Form 1040 line 12e over 12,000 (single, married filing separately, head of household) or 16,000 (married filing jointly), reduced by any Schedule A state income tax already added back on line 2. No schema field holds an addback.

Qualified business income deduction addback (DR 0104 line 3, PDF p.8): the section 199A deduction is added back when AGI exceeds 500,000 (1,000,000 joint), and for partners or shareholders of an entity that made a SALT Parity Election. State income tax addback (line 2): any state income tax deducted on Schedule A. Neither is held by a schema field.

Rate: 'The income tax rate is currently 4.4%. Full-year residents should refer to the tax table in this booklet' (PDF p.10, Line 13). The tax table (PDF p.34-35, '2025 Colorado Income Tax Table with tax rate of 4.4%') has no filing-status columns, and the worksheet for taxable incomes over 50,000 multiplies by .044 (PDF p.35). So one flat bracket from 0 for every status; married_separate and head_of_household are not given separately because no separate schedule is printed. 'Currently' is the booklet's word. The worksheet's caption reads 'Colorado Taxable Income from Form 104 line 11' where the line instructions say line 12 (as printed).

Social Security: relief. DR 0104AD lines 3 and 5 subtract 'Social Security Benefits (including SSDI) received that were included in Federal Taxable Income' (DR 0104AD p.1). Age 65 or older at December 31, 2025: the entire taxable amount. Age 55-64: the entire amount if single with federal AGI (DR 0104 line 34) not over 75,000 or married filing jointly not over 95,000, otherwise limited to 20,000. Under 55: only benefits received due to the death of the person originally entitled to them, limited to 20,000 (PDF p.18 Line 3; PDF p.19 Line 5).

The booklet prints the 55-64 thresholds only for single (75,000) and married filing jointly (95,000). For head of household and married filing separately no threshold is printed; read literally ('if either: Your filing status was single ... or ... married filing jointly'), such a filer qualifies only for the 20,000-limited subtraction, but the booklet does not say so outright. Not found in the booklet.

The 55-64 Social Security rule is two alternative entries in one best_of_group: the full-amount entry is removed above the AGI threshold, the 20,000-limited entry is the alternative. Below the threshold the full entry is never smaller, so best-of gives the printed result.

Pension and annuity subtraction (DR 0104AD lines 4 and 6, PDF p.18-19): the instructions say 'the income you earned from a pension or annuity' that is included in federal taxable income, with no limit by payer: they do not split public from private pensions, or Colorado's own government pensions from federal or other states' government pensions. The form line reads 'Pension, Annuity, IRA, or Disability Income (not including SSDI)'. So one entry per age tier covers public_pension, public_pension_other_state, private_pension, annuity, ira_distribution and employer_plan_distribution. Disability income is named on the form line but no schema income kind holds it.

Pensions from other states' governments: the booklet names no state, prints no reciprocity rule and makes no payer-state distinction; such a pension is in the same entries as Colorado's own (public_pension_other_state in covers), read from the absence of any Colorado-only limit on 'pension or annuity'. No paying_states.

The pension cap is shared with the Social Security subtraction: 24,000 (65 or older) or 20,000 (55-64, or under 55 as a secondary beneficiary) minus the amount entered on line 3, or the person's taxable pension/annuity income if smaller (cap_rule). Each spouse qualifies separately; 'Pension/annuity income should not be intermingled between spouses' (PDF p.19).

Roth conversions are not mentioned (covers_unclear). Military retirement pay of a person 55 or older: the line 4 text names no military pensions and line 7 gives a separate 15,000 subtraction only to people 54 or younger; whether line 4 takes military retirement at 55 or older is not found in the booklet (covers_unclear).

The DR 0104PN part-year schedule (PDF p.65, line 12) takes 'the sum of all income from your federal form 1040, lines 4b, 5b, and 6b', and line 31 (PDF p.68) places 'The pension/annuity subtraction and the PERA or DPS retirement subtraction to the extent included on line 13'; this supports the pension subtraction taking IRA (4b) and pension and annuity (5b) income.

The booklet refers to the Department publication 'Income Tax Topics: Social Security, Pensions and Annuities' for joint returns where both spouses receive Social Security, for the pension subtraction, and for whether and how much of a PERA/DPSRS pension may be subtracted (line 14). That page could not be fetched (fetch.json ok false, timeout), so the PERA/DPSRS amount and the joint-return detail are not found in the sources. Line 14 refers to 'your 2024 federal taxable income' (as printed).

Railroad Benefit Subtraction (line 15, PDF p.22): 'List any railroad retirement benefits that you reported on your federal income tax return and is calculated as part of your federal taxable income'; no age test or cap is printed.
U.S. Government Interest (line 2, PDF p.18): interest on U.S. government bonds, treasury bills and other U.S. obligations; Fannie Mae and Ginnie Mae interest excluded.

Municipal interest (DR 0104 line 9, PDF p.10): 'Interest earned from bonds issued by any state or political subdivision, but not bonds issued by the State of Colorado or its political subdivisions on or after May 1, 1980' is added back. Colorado bonds issued before May 1, 1980 are therefore added back too; the treatment is recorded as other_states_taxed_own_exempt with that exception in the note.
Capital gains: no different rate or deducted share is printed; the agricultural land capital gain subtraction (line 9, capped 100,000) is recorded as a relief, so capital_gains is empty.
Recapture: none found in the booklet; one flat rate.
Indexing: the booklet says nothing about inflation adjustment of the rate or the subtraction caps (not_stated).

Not recorded as reliefs (not retirement or Social Security relief): state tax refund (1), CollegeInvest (10) and ABLE (11) contributions, charitable contributions (12), reservation income (13), marijuana and natural medicine business deduction (16), reacquisition of residency during active duty (17), home savings account (18), FAMLI benefits (19), other (20), HB21-1002 carryforward (21).
